data.gender_notes: Armillia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Armillia is derived from the Latin word 'arma' meaning 'soldier' and 'millia' meaning 'thousands'. This name was given to girls who were dedicated to the service of God in the early Christian Church. They were often called 'Soldier of God' or 'God's Army'. The name Armillia carries the meaning “Soldier of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Armillia usually hope their child will grow to embody soldier of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Armilia was a name given to Christian virgin girls who were dedicated to the service of God in the early Christian Church. These girls lived a life in chastity and devoted themselves to prayer, fasting, and charitable works. They were known as the 'nobilissima órdo' or the 'most noble order' and wore the violet colored tunic, a veil covering their head, and a simple ring as symbols of their commitment. The name Armillia reflects the courage, commitment, and strength of these women in serving God and following His teachings. It is believed that the inspiration for the naming of these girls came from the Roman soldiers who protected and revered the Christians during their persecution.
data.spiritual_significance: Armillia is a name rich in spiritual meaning, symbolizing devotion, commitment, and service to God. It is a reminder of the courage and strength of the early Christian virgin girls who dedicated their lives to serving God and following His teachings. The name connects the bearer to the legacy of these women who lived a life in chastity, prayer, and charitable works, and inspires her to embody their spiritual virtues. It also serves as a reminder of the protection and guidance of God, comparable to the protection of a soldier by his armor. This name is not only a beautiful and meaningful one but also a call to live a life of faith, commitment, and service to God.
